text:
ashwin: FYI noticing sustained queues on the rerank priority lane in us-west-2, while embeddings lanes are mostly idle. latency SLO for rerank is spiking.
infra-bot: alert: queue_length.rerank_priority.us-west-2 = 482 (threshold 200) | gpu_util.us-west-2 = 72% | embedding_lane_idle=18% | time=2026-03-18T09:12:03Z
claire: Is this the per-tenant quota enforcement kicking in or an upstream fanout pattern? Any single customer dumping a ton of low-cost rerank jobs?
ashwin: Looks multi-tenant. The slow part is egress/serialization from rerank workers — they block KV cache hot paths and backpressure cascades to the routing layer, so embeddings traffic gets deprioritized in the same host pool.
ben: Could be head-of-line blocking. Are rerank + embed sharing the same allocation pool? I thought we split by "vector" and "similarity" lanes.
olivia: We do split logical lanes but physical packing sometimes collocates both lanes on same machine for space efficiency. That helps cost but makes backpressure noisy.
claire: Ok. Short-term: we should throttle rerank admission at the edge and apply per-lane smoothing to avoid bursts. Medium-term: stronger isolation (pools) or preemptible rerank instances.
ashwin: Agreed. Proposed immediate patch: add a token-bucket per-lane at the router with dynamic refill based on GPU occupancy metric `gpu_queue_ratio`.
ben: Sketch of config I tested locally:
```
admission:
  lanes:
    rerank_priority:
      algorithm: token_bucket
      capacity: 1000
      refill_per_sec: max(1, floor(100 * (1 - gpu_queue_ratio)))
    embeddings:
      algorithm: token_bucket
      capacity: 2000
      refill_per_sec: 50
```
olivia: That refill formula is nice — it reduces rerank throughput when GPUs are saturated. But watch for sudden drop causing client-side retries -> thundering herd.
claire: We can emit `Retry-After` headers and return a light-weight `429` with a suggested backoff jitter. Also add a 5s queue hop window to absorb small spikes.
ashwin: Also propose a temporary prioritization rule: if `gpu_util` > 85% and `rerank_qps` > threshold, move small embeddings (<200 tokens) to best-effort lane with explicit drop probability.
infra-bot: deploybot: rollout started for router/admission v2 to canary cohort (10% of traffic) at 2026-03-18T09:25Z
sre-oncall: Watch latency p50/p95 for both lanes. If p95_rerank > 800ms for 5m, abort and rollback.
ben: Cost note — isolating lanes to dedicated pools reduces noisy neighbor but increases idle GPU hours. Need to quantify: estimated +12% infra cost for 25% fewer packings.
olivia: For telemetry, add a histogram for per-request wait_in_queue_ms and a gauge for lane_refill_rate. That lets us correlate refill drops with client retries.
claire: I'll open a quick runbook: steps to throttle, add retry header, and rollback criteria. If canary looks good, we schedule wider rollout tonight.
ashwin: Thanks — I'll flip the canary and keep a watch channel. If anyone sees cross-region egress spike (eu-west->us-west) call it out; that can mask as local saturation.
infra-bot: metrics snapshot uploaded: https://graphs.redwood.ai/d/abcd123/rerank-lane-2026-03-18 (contains qlen, gpu_util, p95 latencies)
olivia: Also adding a short-term mitigator: cap concurrent rerank requests per-host to 32 and enable preemptible embed micro-workers on idle slots.
ashwin: Let's reconvene after 30m with canary numbers. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
